ai_summary: CRITICAL POSTURE ALERT: Network analysis identified high-severity cryptographic vulnerabilities resulting in a Risk Score of 55/100. Key risks include unencrypted email transmissions and non-compliant protocol negotiations. Immediate implementation of TLS 1.3 and STARTTLS enforcement is strongly advised to prevent data leakage.

findings.title: SSL 3.0 Detected (POODLE Vulnerable)
findings.description: SSL 3.0 was detected in 11 handshake(s). SSL 3.0 is vulnerable to the POODLE attack (CVE-2014-3566) and has been deprecated since RFC 7568 (2015).
findings.remediation:
1. Disable SSL 3.0 on all mail servers immediately
2. Configure minimum TLS version to 1.2
3. Test with: openssl s_client -connect mail.example.com:465 -tls1_2
findings.ai_explanation: Deprecated cryptographic protocols (SSL 3.0, TLS 1.0/1.1) lack modern cipher suites and are susceptible to protocol-downgrade attacks and cryptanalytic vulnerabilities (e.g., POODLE, BEAST). Modern standards mandate TLS 1.2+.

findings.title: Weak Certificate Signature Algorithm
findings.description: 1 certificate(s) use weak signature algorithms (MD5/SHA-1). These are vulnerable to collision attacks.
findings.evidence: Affected: 1.2.840.113549.1.9.1=www@snakeoil.dom,CN=www.snakeoil.dom,OU=Webserver Team,O=Snake Oil\, Ltd,L=Snake Town,ST=Snake Desert,C=XY
findings.remediation:
1. Re-issue certificates with SHA-256 or stronger
2. Update CA signing configuration
3. Verify: openssl x509 -in cert.pem -text | grep 'Signature Algorithm'
findings.ai_explanation: The observed cryptographic parameters deviate from NIST SP 800-52r2 guidelines, creating security exposure in transport layer integrity and confidentiality.

findings.title: Insufficient Certificate Key Size
findings.description: 1 certificate(s) have key sizes below recommended minimums. Small keys are vulnerable to brute-force factorization.
findings.evidence: 1.2.840.113549.1.9.1=www@snakeoil.dom,CN=www.snakeoil.dom,OU=Webserver Team,O=Snake Oil\, Ltd,L=Snake Town,ST=Snake Desert,C=XY (1024 bits, min 2048)
findings.remediation:
1. Use RSA keys >= 2048 bits (4096 recommended)
2. Use ECC keys >= 256 bits
3. Re-issue certificates with stronger keys
findings.ai_explanation: The observed cryptographic parameters deviate from NIST SP 800-52r2 guidelines, creating security exposure in transport layer integrity and confidentiality.
